title: PAN's Olivia Garza Elected to Head Congreso CDMX's Mesa Directiva for Legislature's Final Year
detail: Deputy Olivia Garza de los Santos (PAN), backed by her own bloc and the allied PVEM, was elected president of the Congreso CDMX's Mesa Directiva with 56 votes, taking over from outgoing PVEM coordinator Jesús Sesma for the III Legislature's third and final year (through August 31, 2027). Garza, who served as Mesa Directiva vice president the prior term, pledged impartial rule enforcement — 'Escucharé a todos, pero no beneficiaré a nadie' — and said the body belongs to the Congress's 66 deputies, not to any single party or majority coalition, promising to balance minority participation against majority rule as the chamber opens its last ordinary legislative year.

title: Brugada's Second Government Report Delivered to Congreso CDMX: 3,000+ Public Works, In-Person Address Set for Oct 14
detail: Secretario de Gobierno César Cravioto delivered Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada's Second Government Report to the Congreso CDMX on her behalf — Brugada instead attended President Claudia Sheinbaum's own second federal report at Palacio Nacional. The four-document package (general report, executive summary, statistical annex, and a per-borough report) is organized around seven axes — welfare and rights, security and resilience, economic prosperity, urban development and housing, sustainability and mobility, cultural pluralism, and participatory/digital governance — and cites more than 3,000 completed public works, 13,000 new or in-progress housing units, 450 km of repaved roads (MXN 4B), 600 km of upgraded 'safe routes for women' (MXN 3B), 643 water and drainage projects (MXN 7B+), 140 km of new Metrobús/Trolebús/Cablebús/tren ligero routes, 777 renovated public schools, and 316 new or refurbished soccer fields. Brugada will personally present and defend the report before Congress on October 14, followed by cabinet-level briefings.
